findings.evidence: grep -c gaPointMul: ChevalleyRelations.lean 5 occurrences (`gaPointMul f g` twice, `gaPointMul_apply_ι` once); no other file in TauCeti/ mentions it.
findings.fix: Keep `gaPointMul`, `gaPointsMulEquiv_gaPointMul` and `gaPointMul_apply_ι`; drop the other six lemmas until a target needs them.
findings.issue: Of the nine new `gaPointMul` declarations, only `gaPointMul_apply_ι` is consumed anywhere (grep: `gaPointMul` occurs only in AdditiveGroup/Basic.lean and ChevalleyRelations.lean; the latter uses `gaPointMul` and `gaPointMul_apply_ι` alone). `mapValue_gaPointMul`, `gaPointMul_one_left/right`, `gaPointMul_comm`, `gaPointMul_assoc`, `gaPointMul_mul_left/right` re-derive the ring axioms of `A` through the points equivalence and serve no roadmap target; the PR's own stated purpose (the commutator relation) does not use them.

findings.evidence: grep '^theorem' TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ChevalleyRelations.lean → two theorems, lines 66 and 87; Transvection.lean:36 states the chosen orientation gives structure constant `1`.
findings.fix: Correct the description to what is proved (one orientation), or add the reversed-orientation statement.
findings.issue: The description claims the PR "proves both orientations of the three-index type-A commutator relation (including the `-1` structure constant)". The new file contains exactly two theorems, `commute_rootSubgroupPoints` and one commutator relation `commutatorElement_rootSubgroupPoints` (hij, hjl, hil); no reversed orientation and no `-1` constant appears in the diff or anywhere in the repo.

summary: The GLₙ transport is in scope: both matrix-level relations already exist on main (TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Transvection.lean), and the merged RootSubgroup.lean explicitly frames transporting them to the functor of points as the completion of that worked example on the Layer 9 path. But the PR also lands a ring-structure theory of 𝔾ₐ-point parameters that nothing needs, and the description overstates what is proved.
